drivingQuestion: When R' Yehuda says the morning prayer may be recited until four hours, is the fourth hour itself included?
outcomeNote: The unit breaks off mid-argument at the end of 26b — the text stops at אלא אי אמרת עד ועד בכלל, רבי יהודה — so the knock-down of the inclusive reading is not contained in this packet.

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל, אוֹ דִילְמָא עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל?! תָּא שְׁמַע רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה. אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל — הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבָּנַן. אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
segments.en: We learned in the mishna that «Rabbi Yehuda says:» The morning prayer may be recited «until four hours» of the day. «A dilemma was raised before» the yeshiva students: When Rabbi Yehuda says «until,» does he mean «until and including» the fourth hour, «or, perhaps» when he says «“until”» he means «until and not including,» in which case one may not pray during the fourth hour? «Come and hear» a resolution to this dilemma based on the mishna. «Rabbi Yehuda says:» The afternoon prayer may be recited only «until the midpoint of the afternoon.» Now, «granted, if you say» that «until» means «until and not including, then there is» a difference «between» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda and» the opinion of «the Rabbis. However, if you say» that «until» means «until and including,» then the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda»
